d54f14326f5bca1f1d7b.text: Express one’s beliefs or convictions based on a material viewed

52b49e33e7ad775e8bdc.text: After going through this module, you are expected to:

41cb0cce30da979ac411.text: 1. differentiate belief from conviction; 2. familiarize expressions in stating beliefs/convictions; 3. communicate beliefs/convictions according to one’s culture and experiences; and 4. express one’s beliefs/convictions based on a material viewed.

2a3d77462ddb5cf23c51.text: Answer each question by choosing the letter of the best answer. Write the answers in your answer sheet. 1. What is expressed in the following sentence?

f13b4e6312cb1850a71e.text: I personally believe that things happen for a reason, so I try to be positive even in difficult times. a. belief b. conclusion c. fact d. reality

932c50b6552cf4424f65.text: 2. What kind of statement is exemplified below?

6e0b804fe1bc5c02534b.text: I think we must really follow basic health protocols like wearing of face masks and face shields and maintaining social distancing because they help prevent Covid 19 from spreading and infecting more people. a. belief b. conclusion c. conviction d. reality

3582bf7728c2399e69e6.text: pictures, posters, videos, and other graphics. People are more likely to believe findings when ideas are paired with visual materials that support the text. In this lesson, we will communicate our beliefs or convictions based on materials viewed.

8e46fdfc8bd14ffa8ba8.text: *What are beliefs and convictions?   *What words, phrases or expressions do  we usually use in expressing our beliefs  and convictions?

e51a15ce629886b38806.text: BELIEF is something that an individual considers as the truth. It is shaped by the

16ebc808d0f4ac2dfe2c.text: individual’s background experiences and is based on one’s cultural or personal faith, morality, or values.

31730c8044ba8f02ad53.text: CONVICTION is a firm belief on something that an individual is convinced of. To be

303e2cebe44a8a4a92ec.text: convinced you need to obtain all related information like

4579569e09db4c73d507.text:  statistical data - based on analysis of statistics;  observational data - based on what the person has observed or perceived they observed  causal data - based on what fact has caused a particular factual result; and  experiential data - based on what experience shows can be inferred from the facts. A conviction remains the same even with new experiences and even after long periods of time because it is built in concrete information.

0fd797fd50fb38929ff8.text: Basic Signal Phrases in Expressing Beliefs or Convictions

labels.text: My point of view is that…

eeae1406f655166fe760.text:  I feel…   I think…   I believe that…   In my opinion…   From my point of view…   In my view…   I really feel that…   Personally, I think…   Personally speaking…   My point of view is that…

b572694c9ebd3685a504.text: photographs, cinema, cartoons, prints, designs and three-dimensional art such as sculpture and architecture.

afe41d1fea568985c27f.text: facts, relationships, inferences, and to critical analysis. Understanding visual images can connect to accompanying spoken or written language like expressing your own beliefs or convictions to a particular subject.

b85df4abe47faa6d79cb.text: Video gives you a chance to show stimulating visual information. Use video to

fbfa6e0f6380868776aa.text: bring movement, pictures and sound into your presentation. Always make sure that the clip is directly relevant to your content. Tell your audience what to look for. Avoid showing any more film than you need.

5ba08b7605481c90d8cd.text: Drawing is creating a picture with a variety of tools like pencils, crayons, pens

4e1c412306e461283eeb.text: or markers. Artists draw on different types of surfaces, like paper or canvas.

fd94a76737ead90f992e.text: Painting is often called the most important form of visual art. It is about

f7611d5dd45faad72a67.text: putting colors on a canvas or a wall. Painters express their ideas through a mixture of colors and different brush strokes. It is also one of the oldest forms of visual arts.

4aeda4893db5d6418851.text: Photography is making pictures by letting light pass through the lenses of a

c32ce76e060b35bc903b.text: camera onto a film. Images could then be printed onto special paper.

77fbb11b2889df82c090.text: Today, most photography is digital. Cameras have no film; the images are

ae45727f663952c1a974.text: Filmmaking is the process of directing and producing movies for television and

e7262944308d9511e1c7.text: cinemas. It is a very expensive and complicated form of art, involving many tasks, for example scriptwriting, casting and editing film sequences before they can be shown to an audience.

74027e33ac2317e25cbb.text: Sculptures are three-dimensional pieces of art that are created by shaping

632a55c6d7b0dbc03518.text: various kinds of material. Among the popular sculpting materials are steel, plastic, ceramics and wood. Sculpture is often referred to as plastic arts.

09ca38f8643c1fe1441e.text: Cartoon is a type of illustration, sometimes animated, typically in a non-

41bc6070dce662de5ee9.text: realistic or semi-realistic style. Cartoons are drawings and illustrations that come in several forms and can have many meanings. One type of cartoon is drawings and illustrations in magazines or newspapers. Another type is animated or audio-visual cartoon films that contain sound, voices and attractive animated drawings. As a result, a cartoon film can be close to real life, because visual clues and contexts can make it possible to view the messages as much more real especially as the viewers can listen to the voice overs.

1aff4a2746f589dc499e.text: Let us further develop your critical thinking skills through the activity below. Write a short paragraph expressing your own beliefs/convictions on the issues presented in the following photographs and images.

7f44567d030db0934e88.text: A. Directions: Read carefully the short conversation. Copy the sentences that state a belief/conviction and underlined the expressions used.

33d9e2fd93f1c6b698dc.text: Mario: Lucio, what do you think makes a good friend? Lucio: Well for me, I think a friend is someone who is fun to be with. Mario: Hmmm…fun to be with? Can you give me an example? Lucio: I would say that I like friends who like to go out and have fun together –go downtown, go to the beach, see a movie, something like that. Mario: So, does that mean a friend has to like the same things you do? Lucio: No…not really, I just believe that we will easily become friends right away if we have the same hobbies and they are fun to be with.
